sentences.text:
Ramprasad vs The New India Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 April, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Ind:8875
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Binod Kumar Dwivedi
 On The 6 th Of April, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 4811 of 2018
 Ramprasad
 Versus
 The New India Insurance Co. Ltd And Others
 Appearance:
Shri Balkrishna Royal - Advocate appearing on behalf of
- Advocate for appellant.

Shri Pradip Kumar Gupta - Advocate for respondent No.1 
 Company.

Order 
This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
against the impugned award dated 31/07/2018 passed by I Additional Member, Motor Accident
Claims Tribu

nal, Dhar (M.P.) in Claim Case No.241/2017, whereby an amount of Rs.81,104/- has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition i.e. 21/0/2017 to the appellant / injured with interest @ 6% per annum.
2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the amount awarded by the learned Claim Tribunal is on lower side looking to the injuries suffered by the claimant.
Appellant has suffered fracture of radius in right hand wrist.

Dr. Devendra Mandloi (AW-2) has given 18% permanent disability, which has not been taken into consideration by the learned Claims NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8875 2 MA-4811-2018 Tribunal, which has resulted in lower amount of compensation, therefore, learned counsel submits that at least Rs.30,000/- more should have been given, which will be just and proper compensation.
On this ground learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount as prayed for.

3 . Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.1 / Insurance Company opposed the prayer on the ground that amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the compensation amount.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

sentences.text: 5. It is not in dispute that appellant has suffered fracture of radius in right hand wrist and has suffered other injuries also.

Dr. Devendra Mandloi (AW-2) has been examined to prove the Permanent Disability Certificate (Ex.-P/14) but the fact remains that the appellant has not suffered any functional disability, therefore, looking to the nature of injuries, this Court is of the view that if at least a lump sum amount of Rs.30,000/- is awarded over and above the amount already awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal, the same will sub serve the ends of justice.

6. Hence, without going into the nicety of the computation of the amount, the amount is enhanced and appellant / injured is entitled to an additional lump sum amount of Rs.30,000/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8875 3 MA-4811-2018 7.
Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellant is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.
The other terms and conditions of the impugned award including the interest part shall remain intact.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE Tej Ramprasad vs The New India Insurance Co. Ltd on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/96887438/
